_meta.description: Competitor playbook. Recommendations are analytical judgments grounded in the evidence fields.

domains.opportunity: Reach frontier parity where it is monetized (agentic coding, long-horizon tasks); be 'good enough' and cheap everywhere else.
domains.evidence: >80% of Anthropic's Q3 revenue came from models <6 months old; coding users spend ~20×.
domains.target: Developers and engineering orgs; agentic platforms
domains.capabilities: Frontier coding model + long-context agent training; fast release cadence
domains.action: Ship a coding-specialized frontier tier on a 3–4-month cadence; publish per-task cost vs Opus 5.5 on public harnesses.
domains.benefit: Contest the highest-value workloads where switching happens every release.
domains.risk: Parity is costly; a near-miss buys nothing.
domains.metric: Share of SWE agent workloads on own model (SWE-bench Pro, internal routing logs).

domains.opportunity: Price per completed task, not per token; attack where Anthropic's surge costs are highest.
domains.evidence: ~$600M of Q3 price cuts; 2× list-price premium over GPT-6.1 Sol held share; Q3 surge premium $5.0B.
domains.target: High-volume agent pipelines; cost-sensitive enterprise workloads
domains.capabilities: Effort controls, caching, routing; verifiable task-level benchmarks
domains.action: Offer outcome-based or per-task guarantees on reference workloads; bundle capacity guarantees in surge periods.
domains.benefit: Turns Anthropic's capacity timing risk into a customer-facing reliability advantage.
domains.risk: Margin dilution if price elasticity is low.
domains.metric: Win rate on price-sensitive RFPs; cost per task vs Claude.

domains.opportunity: Own the developer loop (repo, CI, review) and make the model swappable inside it.
domains.evidence: GitHub agents start ~40% of PRs (Octoverse); Copilot Fusion routing; Claude Code 'default' in many enterprises.
domains.capabilities: Agent harness, sandboxes, repo context, review tooling
domains.action: Integrate deeply with source control and CI; offer enterprise policy, audit and cost controls for multi-model agents.
domains.benefit: Shifts loyalty from model to platform.
domains.risk: Developers prefer best model; routing perceived as downgrade.
domains.metric: Agent-authored PRs on own platform; seats with consumption add-ons.

domains.opportunity: Differentiate on the agent runtime: identity, permissions, memory, long-running sandboxes and governance.
domains.evidence: Anthropic sells Managed Agents, Agent SDK, MCP; Enterprise Frontier Safeguards built with >100 customers.
domains.capabilities: Identity/permissions, data residency, audit, persistent compute
domains.action: Offer a governed agent runtime that runs any frontier model, with customer-held keys and residency.
domains.benefit: Captures value regardless of which model wins a release cycle.
domains.risk: Anthropic's own runtime is already enterprise-grade.
domains.metric: Agents in production per customer; hours of autonomous work governed.

domains.opportunity: Use productivity suites and marketplaces to embed agents where work happens, but don't count on resale fees.
domains.evidence: CSP-marketplace share fell to ≈40% in Q3; channel terms renegotiated; Copilot Cowork built on Claude.
domains.capabilities: Suite integration; consumption billing inside bundles
domains.action: Bundle agent consumption into suite agreements with pooled credits; make first-party models the default with frictionless BYO-model.
domains.benefit: Monetizes the <0.1% wallet-share gap Anthropic cites.
domains.risk: Customers demand Claude inside the suite.

domains.opportunity: Convert infrastructure advantage into customer-level cost and capacity guarantees.
domains.evidence: Anthropic paid a premium for $5.0B of surge compute; $213.8B of its commitments depend on suppliers' financing.
domains.target: Frontier labs and large AI-native customers
domains.capabilities: Spare capacity, investment-grade financing, chip roadmaps
domains.action: Sell reserved surge capacity and chip-financing packages; price capacity insurance for demand spikes.
domains.benefit: Earns rent from rivals' growth regardless of model share.

domains.opportunity: Go where Anthropic is thin: regulated industries outside software, mid-market, and regions needing sovereignty.
domains.evidence: Ode with Anthropic targets mid-market; international 29% of revenue; seven vertical solutions only.
domains.target: Banks, insurers, manufacturers, public sector, APAC enterprises
domains.capabilities: FDE teams, SI alliances, in-region capacity
domains.action: Stand up industry FDE pods with SIs; offer in-country inference and data residency by default.
domains.benefit: Captures depth before standardization locks in.
domains.risk: Long sales cycles; SIs also partner with Anthropic.
domains.metric: Production deployments per vertical; regional revenue.

google.title: The Google lens: Anthropic is Google Cloud's best customer and Gemini's toughest competitor

points.view: Anthropic is the anchor external TPU customer: ≈$121.3B CSP minimum + ≈$161.2B Broadcom-financed TPU leases + $125–150B additional TPU estimate. Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B in Q3 with a $561B backlog.
points.incentive: Maximize Anthropic's TPU consumption; TPU sales win regardless of model share.
points.tension: Every Anthropic token served on TPU strengthens a Gemini rival.

points.view: Google 2026 NPA (up to $20B, reduced by up to $10B if Google buys IPO-concurrent shares); ownership cap 14.99%; reported up-to-$40B investment plan.
points.tension: Investor upside vs first-party model share.

points.view: Claude sold on Vertex AI; Anthropic is shrinking marketplace share (≈40% Q3) and renegotiated channel terms.
points.tension: Fee capture per Anthropic dollar is falling.

points.view: Menlo: Google 9% of enterprise LLM API spend (from 21%) vs Anthropic 55%. Gemini 4 Argon at $2/$10 intro rising to $4/$20.
points.incentive: Win frontier share and Workspace attach.
points.tension: Price parity at the frontier hasn't moved share; capability in coding is the gap.

points.view: Workspace distribution + Gemini app 1B MAU; Antigravity replaced Gemini CLI.
points.incentive: Own the knowledge-work interface where Cowork competes.
points.tension: Cowork and Claude for Microsoft 365 target the same users.

actions: Separate scorecards: Google Cloud should be measured on total Anthropic-related compute + TPU revenue; Gemini on first-party API and Workspace agent share — avoid letting one suppress the other.
Offer Anthropic reserved surge TPU capacity at a premium (Q3 shows willingness to pay) while prioritizing Gemini for internal frontier runs.
Close the coding gap first: make Antigravity + Gemini competitive on long-horizon agentic coding, the category that drives ~20× user intensity.
Use Workspace as the agent runtime for knowledge work with pooled consumption credits — compete with Cowork where Google owns the documents.
In APAC/Japan, pair in-region TPU capacity and data residency with SI-led (NEC/Fujitsu/NRI-style) delivery before Claude standardizes in large accounts.

apac.title: APAC and Japan: hypotheses to validate, not market-share estimates
context: Anthropic's international revenue is 29.4% of 9M 2026 (billing address); no country split is disclosed.
Anthropic Japan reports staff 3 → 50+, adopting organizations >10×, usage ~1.9× other countries (Oct 2026 briefing, via press).
Hitachi (~290,000 employees) and NEC (~30,000) are deploying Claude; NRI is the first authorized reseller; the IPO earmarks up to ~$3.5B for Japanese investors.
Japan's government plans up to ¥1T for a sovereign model; Teikoku Databank finds 34.5% of firms use gen AI (63.6% of large firms).

segments.hypothesis: Fastest adopters of consumption-priced coding agents; most price-sensitive and most open-weight-tolerant.
segments.validate: Win/loss on coding-agent pilots; token mix by model class.

segments.hypothesis: Adopt through SIs (NEC, Hitachi, Fujitsu, NRI) and standardize on one primary model per workflow; legacy modernization is the entry point.
segments.validate: SI pipeline by model vendor; modernization project counts.

segments.hypothesis: Data residency and auditability decide; in-region inference is a gating requirement.
segments.validate: RFP requirements on inference residency; regulator guidance.

segments.hypothesis: Agentic engineering (code, CAD, documentation) before shop-floor; physical-AI standards (MCP-style) matter later.
Customer-service and content workloads route to cheaper tiers (Haiku/Flash/open-weight).
Network-ops agents and sovereign hosting; telcos as resellers of in-country capacity.
segments.validate: Telco partnership announcements; sovereign cloud RFPs.

segments.hypothesis: Claude Code adoption mirrors US pattern with a lag; Japanese-language tooling and support matter.
segments.validate: Developer surveys; Claude Code seats in region.

risks: Sovereignty programs and domestic models can mandate local stacks for public sector.
Open-weight models (often Chinese-origin) carry procurement and security concerns that may cut both ways.
Price sensitivity favors routing to cheaper tiers; FDE capacity in-region is scarce.

matrix.note: Analytical judgment on a 1–3 scale for adoption potential (A), competitive intensity (C) and usage economics (E, consumption per user). Not measured data.

signposts.why: Tests whether Q3 was a pause or a new slope.
Margin pressure and supplier pricing power.
Velocity tax on closing the loop.
